FOH.why: Anisah’s customer service is genuinely 10/10. She has an amazing bubbly personality that customers naturally gravitate towards, and her smile is infectious. She consistently approaches customers with warmth and enthusiasm and creates a welcoming atmosphere for everyone she serves. Even when managing her own section, she remains attentive and engaging with her customers. Her positive energy doesn’t just improve the experience of our guests, but also lifts the mood of the team around her. Customer interaction has always been one of her strongest qualities and she represents the friendly and welcoming service we want to provide at M11 extremely well.

Anisah has shown an immense amount of improvement in her efficiency and time management since joining us in March. She is now able to lock in and focus on managing her section effectively whilst simultaneously keeping on top of other responsibilities such as preparing chopsticks and napkins. What has particularly impressed me is the improvement in her ability to think ahead. For example, she now anticipates when we are going to run out of something and asks KP for a new load before it happens. This allows her to remain prepared, reduces interruptions during service and means other team members don’t have to step away from their own sections to assist her. She has become significantly more independent and organised during service, and the progress she has made through consistently asking questions, taking feedback on board and actively working to improve has been amazing to see.
answers.Describe a time when this employee demon: Anisah is always willing and ready to support the people around her, particularly during busy services. When she is running and isn’t responsible for her own section, she is constantly looking for ways to help the rest of the team. In between running food, she will clear tables for team members, help pack Deliveroo orders and step in to greet and seat guests if the host is momentarily occupied. What stands out to me is that she never has the attitude of “that isn’t my job”. If she can see that somebody needs support, she is happy to jump in and help wherever she can. This takes pressure off the rest of the FOH team and helps us maintain a smooth service even when several areas of the restaurant are busy at the same time.
answers.Give us an example of when the employee: Anisah has become really good at recognising what needs to be done without always needing to be directed. A great example is when she is running food during a busy service. Rather than standing and waiting for the next dishes to come up, she uses that time to look around the restaurant and identify where she can help. She may clear and reset a table for another server, pack a Deliveroo order that is waiting or notice guests waiting at the entrance and seat them if the host is busy. She has also developed the initiative to anticipate things before they become an issue, such as noticing when we are running low on chopsticks or napkins and arranging for more before we completely run out. This growing awareness of not just her own responsibilities but what the wider team and restaurant need has been one of the biggest improvements I’ve seen in her.
answers.Give an example that best supports this: Anisah consistently demonstrates a really strong work ethic and can-do attitude. She comes into her shifts ready to work and is always looking for ways she can contribute. She actively asks for feedback on how she can improve and, rather than becoming discouraged when something takes her longer to learn, she puts the time and effort into developing until she gets it. The improvement she has made since joining us in March is a testament to her motivation and willingness to learn. She is also always looking for extra shifts and is regularly one of the first team members to volunteer when additional hours become available.
answers.Provide an example of when the employee: Anisah has developed a great awareness of what needs doing around the restaurant without having to wait for a manager to direct her. When running food, for example, she uses any downtime productively by clearing and resetting tables for other team members, packing Deliveroo orders or stepping in to greet and seat guests when the host is occupied. She has also started anticipating operational needs herself, such as recognising when we are getting low on chopsticks or napkins and asking KP to prepare more before we run out. This has been one of the biggest areas of improvement I’ve seen in her , she is increasingly thinking ahead and taking responsibility for what needs to happen next rather than waiting to be asked.
answers.Has this employee ever missed a shift or: There have been occasions where Anisah has been unable to attend a shift or has been running late, however what stands out is the level of responsibility and communication she demonstrates when this happens. She always lets me know in advance and, where she is unable to attend, she will often come to me having already found a potential solution by asking another team member if they are available to cover her shift, before checking with me that the change is okay. Similarly, if she knows she is going to be late, she communicates this in advance and keeps me informed rather than leaving the management team unaware. She is also willing to stay later where needed to make up the time. Outside of this, Anisah is one of our most reliable team members. She regularly looks for additional shifts, is often one of the first to accept extra hours and is extremely willing to step in when another member of the team calls in sick. Her communication, accountability and willingness to find solutions make her someone I can genuinely rely on.
answers.Describe a time when the employee delive: Anisah has made significant progress in the quality and consistency of her work since joining us. She is now able to confidently manage her own section, keeping on top of her tables whilst also maintaining the smaller details that contribute to a smooth service, such as ensuring her section is clean, organised and properly stocked with chopsticks and napkins. She has particularly improved in anticipating what will be needed during service. Rather than waiting until something has completely run out, she will notice stock getting low and communicate with KP in advance so that more can be prepared. This helps her maintain her section to the expected standard without unnecessary interruptions to service. During particularly busy periods she can occasionally become flustered and make mistakes, so consistency under pressure is still an area she is developing. What I really value, however, is her accountability. If she does make a mistake, she communicates it to management immediately rather than hiding it or allowing the issue to escalate. She understands when something is outside her scope to resolve and involves us so we can communicate appropriately with the customer and BOH. Her ability to take feedback on board, learn from mistakes and actively ask how she can improve is a major reason the overall quality of her work has developed so much.
answers.Please give an example of when this empl: When Anisah encounters an issue during service, she is very good at communicating it rather than trying to hide a mistake or allowing the problem to escalate. If something happens that she is able to resolve within her role, she will take the necessary steps to correct it, and if it is outside of her scope, she knows to notify a manager promptly so that we can step in, communicate with the customer and liaise with BOH where necessary. She has also shown this problem-solving mindset outside of service. If she knows she is unable to attend a shift, she will often proactively speak to another team member about potentially covering it before approaching me, meaning she comes to management with both the problem and a possible solution. Handling pressure during particularly busy periods is still an area she is developing, but her honesty, communication and willingness to ask for support mean issues are identified quickly and can be resolved before they become bigger problems.
answers.Can you provide an example of when the e: One of the biggest improvements I have seen in Anisah is her awareness of the smaller details that help keep service running smoothly. When managing her section, she is now much more conscious of keeping it clean, organised and properly stocked whilst still remaining attentive to her tables. She has developed the ability to anticipate what she will need rather than waiting until something becomes a problem. For example, she will notice when chopsticks or napkins are beginning to run low and communicate with KP to arrange more before we completely run out. She also pays attention to what is happening around her and, when she is running, will notice tables that need clearing, Deliveroo orders that need packing or guests waiting to be seated and step in without needing to be asked. Attention to detail during particularly busy periods is still something she is developing, but she has shown immense improvement since joining us. Importantly, if she notices she has made a mistake, she takes accountability and informs a manager so it can be corrected quickly rather than allowing it to impact the customer or the rest of the service.
answers.Has this employee shown any notable impr: Absolutely. Anisah has shown an immense amount of growth and improvement. When she first joined us, she required more support and direction with managing her time, prioritising tasks and maintaining awareness of everything happening within her section. Since then, and particularly over the past month, I have seen a noticeable increase in her confidence and independence. She is now able to manage her own section much more effectively whilst keeping on top of additional responsibilities, anticipating when things need restocking and supporting other areas of the restaurant without always needing to be prompted. She has gone from needing regular direction to increasingly recognising for herself what needs to be done next. What makes her improvement particularly deserving of recognition is the effort she has put into achieving it. She has never been afraid to ask questions or admit when she doesn’t know something. She actively asks how she can improve, listens to the guidance she is given and genuinely tries to implement it on her next shift. Seeing that feedback translate into noticeable improvements in her confidence, organisation and overall performance has been amazing.
answers.What makes this employee’s performance s: What makes Anisah stand out to me is not that she is perfect, but the amount of growth, effort and determination she has shown. Since joining us in March, she has developed immensely and has consistently demonstrated that she genuinely wants to become better at what she does. She actively asks for feedback, takes it on board and puts it into practice. She has grown from needing additional guidance and support to becoming increasingly confident and independent in managing her own section, anticipating what needs to be done and supporting the wider team without always needing to be asked. Alongside that growth, she has maintained an amazing attitude. Her bubbly personality and infectious smile make her fantastic with customers, she is always willing to help her colleagues, regularly volunteers for additional shifts and is one of the first people willing to step in when we need cover. What stands out most is her willingness to take responsibility. If she makes a mistake, she communicates it. If she needs help, she asks. If she cannot attend a shift, she communicates in advance and will often have already tried to find a solution. She doesn’t shy away from areas she finds difficult; she asks how she can improve and keeps working at them. Anisah still has areas to develop, particularly maintaining her confidence and accuracy under pressure, but the progress she has made through her own effort is exactly why I believe she deserves recognition this month. She has become a genuinely valuable and dependable member of our team, and I am incredibly proud of how far she has come.
